experiments.paper_location: Conference manuscript p6, Section 4.2, Low-rank Approximation; actual orthogonal/cosh/stabilization choices are source variants
experiments.mechanism: Execute maintained positive feature and projection functions on Torch CPU, independently reconstruct raw features and restored kernels with scalar FP64 arithmetic, check analytic input/projection derivatives and projection structural invariants.

conditions.execution: Actual maintained initial source functions on CPU Torch; no replacement feature implementation
conditions.gradient_domain: eps0 and nonlog restored features only; log output and nonzero eps have forward checks only
conditions.oracle: Scalar FP64 exponent/dot/norm feature expression and analytic derivatives, independent of maintained normalization/amax/einsum helpers; structural projection properties without a second QR algorithm
conditions.scope: Cosh and noncosh, query/key stabilizers, temperatures, eps/log boundaries, finite small inputs, FP32/FP64 numerical budgets; all actual/reference/errors explicitly finite
conditions.sensitivity: Three executed actual-function arithmetic mutants are rejected
conditions.statistical_limits: Deterministic and projection-structural checks do not prove Gaussian-marginal sampling, independence, entrywise variance bounds, normalized-output unbiasedness or paper model metrics
conditions.lifecycle: Repaired lifecycle has its own SCATTERBRAIN-FEATURE-STATE-CPU regression; arithmetic fixtures use supplied projections, while native composition explicitly freezes an actual sampled projection

experiments.note: The conference main text displays IID-Gaussian features; this release uses optional cosh/orthogonal features and stabilizing log scales. Sampling-law/proof correspondence remains distinct from executed finite arithmetic. Appendix C/D.3 are now inspected with documented assumptions and causal inconsistencies; lifecycle is repaired separately under #106; no GPU/causal/native sanitizer claim is made.

experiments.paper_location: Section4.2 low-rank approximation; maintained feature lifecycle support, not a printed scheduling algorithm
experiments.mechanism: Initialize cold feature maps, honor requested redraw periods, freeze warm deterministic evaluation, persist projection/cadence/period and migrate declared legacy checkpoints while retaining current buffer dtype.

conditions.execution: Actual maintained CPU feature class and unchanged projection sampler
conditions.oracle: Explicit expected draw-request sequences and RNG continuation; independent scalar FP64 raw-feature expressions; serialized checkpoints and invalid metadata nonmutation checks
conditions.rng: Global Torch RNG is caller owned and restored explicitly for identical future draws; it is not part of feature state_dict
conditions.legacy_policy: Projection-only nonzero valid matrices resume warm at counter0/receiver period; old allzero matrices explicitly migrate cold, including shape-ambiguous legacy zeros
conditions.limits: Lifecycle metadata prevalidation is not a general transactional PyTorch load guarantee; no GPU, Gaussian-law, variance or normalized-unbiasedness claim

experiments.note: Constructor consumes no RNG. First draw has counter0; warm explicit requests advance cadence, q/key encoding does not. Positive integral numeric periods and +inf are supported; strings, bools, nonintegral and out-of-range periods are rejected. Five source mutants must fail.
